findings.message: On successful completion, a signal that arrived after the child finished (before restore) is raised from __exit__ after the result was computed. The `return completed` is discarded, so a completed child result is lost and KeyboardInterrupt/ChildCancelled is raised instead. That is arguably intended, but with a signal that arrives during the final finally cleanup it also skips the check for communication_completed and may leave state inconsistent. More importantly, if `handle` set `pending` when `running` was False (e.g. during cleanup), a pending signal is raised even when the original exception is a different one only if exception_type is None, so cancellation is silently dropped when another exception (e.g. CalledProcessError or TimeoutExpired) propagates.
findings.suggestion: When an exception is already propagating and a cancellation is pending, raise the pending cancellation (chaining the original) rather than dropping it, so SIGTERM/SIGINT is never swallowed by a check=True failure.
